LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 WORD CLASSES: COMPOUND SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.3: Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we join sentences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify compound sentences from texts
2. construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions
3. appreciate the usage of compound sentences in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 WORD CLASSES: COMPOUND SENTENCES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 WORD CLASSES: COMPOUND SENTENCES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify compound sentences from texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify compound sentences from texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify compound sentences from texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify compound sentences from texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions

What this means
In this part you learn to construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the usage of compound sentences in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the usage of compound sentences in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the usage of compound sentences in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the usage of compound sentences in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify compound sentences from texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences to a partner. (skill: construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the usage of compound sentences in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify compound sentences from texts.
3. Practise this skill: construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the usage of compound sentences in communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we join sentences?
2. How do we join sentences?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify compound sentences from texts.
5. Be able to: construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
